items.expected-result: the 1.20.0 self-instrumentation records real per-operation metrics and the memory_performance tool reports them; an operation that never ran is absent rather than reported as zero (1.20.0 #327, ADR-0074)
items.command: 5x memory_write + 3x memory_search, then memory_performance(projectId); separately an overflow probe: 1300x memory_watch_status in 3.6s on a fresh bank, then memory_performance after the flush tick
items.evidence:
memory_write count=5 (p50 3.57ms); memory_search count=3 (p50 5.76ms); search.fts/fusion/affinity/snippets/bump all count=3 with distinct non-zero latencies; search.vector count=3 but zero latency ('provider: (none — FTS5-only search)' on this bank).
Every uncalled tool present at count:0 with a full 180-bucket array.
Overflow: 1300 calls in 3.57s -> metrics.flush.batch_size=1000, metrics.dropped=300 (exactly 1300-1000), and the probe's own series count=1000 not 1300.
items.observed-result: Counts and latencies are real, per-operation and accurate. The ADR-0074 capped buffer behaves exactly as designed at the boundary, verified with a genuine overflow rather than inferred. But the item's expected-result is WRONG on one point: an operation that never ran is NOT absent — it is deliberately reported present at count 0 (the WP6 derived-inventory contract, stated in the tool's own MCP description and in PerformanceReport's doc comment). The expected-result cited ADR-0074 for that claim; that ADR is about the buffer mechanism and does not address absent-vs-zero at all.
items.acceptance-reason: Fails against the stated text, which is the honest outcome — but the defect is in the item, not the product. I authored this expected-result for this run and misattributed the absent-vs-zero claim to ADR-0074. The shipped behaviour is correct, intentional and gate-covered. Accepted as a known error in the checklist itself; the corrected expectation is recorded in findings #5 so the next run does not inherit the wrong text.

items.expected-result: the 1.20.0 metrics feature exposes whatever operator-facing configuration it has through a CLI command family, consistent with every other configurable subsystem (1.20.0 #327, ADR-0074)
items.command: ai-raccoon --help; ai-raccoon performance; ai-raccoon metrics; ai-raccoon sweep show (control); read MetricsConfigKeys.cs, MetricsFlusher.cs, CliCommandTree.cs, SettingsCommands.cs, ConfigCommands.cs; grep -rn 'MetricsConfigKeys\.' src
items.evidence:
--help lists 13 families (access, model, retrieval, sweep, noise, queryguard, sync, ingest, watch, encryption, extract, maintenance, serve) — no performance/metrics.
'performance' and 'metrics' -> 'Unrecognized command or argument', exit=9. Control 'sweep show' -> 'enabled: True  interval: 24 h  threshold: 0.3', exit=0.
MetricsConfigKeys.cs defines three live keys: metrics.buffer-capacity.global (1000), metrics.flush-interval-seconds.global (30), metrics.retention-days.global (28).
MetricsFlusher.cs:41,49,179,197 re-read capacity and interval via GetSettingAsync on every flush tick; MaintenanceJobs.cs:163 reads retention the same way.
grep 'MetricsConfigKeys.': reads only — no SetSettingAsync anywhere in the tree. ConfigCommands.cs has no generic 'settings set <key>' escape hatch.
items.observed-result: Metrics has three genuine, live-reconfigurable operator knobs — the same settings-table shape every other subsystem exposes through its own CLI family — and none of the three is reachable from the CLI at all.
items.acceptance-reason: A real product defect, not a design choice: metrics is the only settings-backed configurable subsystem in the codebase with zero CLI exposure, so an operator who is not an agent cannot tune or inspect it short of writing to the settings table by hand. A `performance` family should expose at minimum buffer-capacity, flush-interval and retention set/show, mirroring the shape SettingsCommands.cs already uses for sweep, noise, queryguard, extract and maintenance. Not accepted because nothing tracks it yet; this run is the first to catch it.

items.expected-result: the project's Semantica knowledge graph is reachable and its contents reflect the project — decisions and entities are queryable, or its emptiness has a named cause
items.command: get_graph_summary(); query_decisions(limit=5); read .ai-raccoon/semantica-graph.json + its git history; read the semantica-knowledge-graph skill and export_semantica_graph.py; grep for any CI/hook wiring of semantica; count docs/adr
items.evidence:
get_graph_summary -> {"node_count":0,"decision_count":0,"graph_ready":true}; query_decisions -> {"decisions":[]}
.ai-raccoon/semantica-graph.json (one commit, 7fa70e07) contains {"nodes":[],"edges":[],"decisions":[]} — the export script's DEFAULT_SEED. File and live graph AGREE; no disagreement to report.
Project skill: 'session-scoped ... do not survive a process restart'; Gotchas: 'in-memory graph dies on process exit. No import_graph mechanism exists.'
docs/adr holds 74 files; no CI workflow or repo script populates Semantica.
items.observed-result: The graph is reachable — both tools respond correctly — but structurally cannot hold cross-session content: it is in-memory and session-scoped by design with no import path, so any fresh session starts at zero regardless of the 74 ADRs. The one artifact meant to bridge sessions was itself committed already empty, so the export tooling has never been exercised with real content — and could not be loaded back even if it had been.
items.acceptance-reason: Emptiness is the correct state for this architecture and the cause is named rather than the symptom re-reported. Secondary observation for follow-up, not a failure of this item: graph_ready:true reads as 'server operational', not 'populated', so a never-used graph and a failed-to-load graph report identically — an operator cannot tell them apart from this flag alone.

summary.note: Of the three failures, exactly one is a product defect: perf-metrics-cli-surface. One is a defect in the checklist's own tooling (full-mcp-surface, caused by derive-facts.sh miscounting), and one is a defect in an expected-result I wrote for this run (perf-metrics-self-instrumentation). No item was left with a null `accepted`.

findings-against-prior-runs.finding: derive-facts.sh, the script that exists to stop hand-typed counts going stale, itself reports a wrong count.
findings-against-prior-runs.detail: Its grep for `\[McpServerTool` matches a /// doc comment at src/AiRaccoon/Tools/McpToolInventory.cs:7 that names the attribute because that file implements the reflection-based inventory. Loose pattern: 28. Attribute-only pattern: 27. Live server: 27. A derived number that is wrong is more dangerous than a typed one because it carries the authority of having been measured. Fixed upstream in an ai-badger PR with a red-first regression test.

findings-against-prior-runs.finding: That miscount manufactured a phantom feature.
findings-against-prior-runs.detail: Because the count moved 26 -> 28, this run's brief told a lane to find 'the two new tools since 1.19.1'. Only one was added: memory_performance (#327). The lane cross-checked the tree, a fresh v1.19.1 checkout, and the live server, and reported the premise as false rather than adjusting its expectation to fit — which is the behaviour the skill asks for.

findings-against-prior-runs.finding: Two documented event ids are dead.
findings-against-prior-runs.detail: 512 (Vacuum) and 516 (VacuumDeferred) have no call site anywhere in src: ADR-0070 moved vacuuming into MaintenanceJobRunner, which logs 525 instead. They can never fire. Documented ids that cannot fire are the same defect shape as a checklist step for a removed feature. Marked as retired in docs/reference/logging-event-ids.md by this PR rather than deleted, so the numbers are not silently reused.

findings-against-prior-runs.finding: Event ids 10-12 are documented against the wrong file.
findings-against-prior-runs.detail: The reference names src/AiRaccoon/Program.cs; the [LoggerMessage] methods live in src/AiRaccoon/AppRunner.cs (Program.cs is a four-line shim). Pre-existing, unrelated to 1.20.0. Corrected by this PR.

findings-against-prior-runs.finding: An expected-result written for this run was wrong, and the run recorded it as a failure rather than quietly fixing it.
findings-against-prior-runs.detail: perf-metrics-self-instrumentation asserted 'an operation that never ran is absent rather than reported as zero' and cited ADR-0074. The shipped contract is the opposite and deliberate — every tool always appears at count 0 (WP6 derived-inventory gate) — and ADR-0074 does not address the question at all. CORRECTED TEXT for the next run: 'the 1.20.0 self-instrumentation records real per-operation metrics and the memory_performance tool reports them; every tool in the derived inventory appears in the report, at count 0 when unused, and measurements past the buffer cap are dropped with the dropped count recorded (1.20.0 #327; buffer per ADR-0074)'.

findings-against-prior-runs.finding: The 1.19.1 run's 'substituted' verdict on the maintenance re-sweep was defeatable.
findings-against-prior-runs.detail: It reported that chunk-backfill is once-per-bank and consumed by the automatic startup pass, so the re-sweep could not be driven live. Re-derived per step 4: the CLI-only command path builds a DI container without the maintenance hosted service, so `maintenance list` migrates the bank without running a pass. Seeding an oversized row in that window let this run observe the re-sweep directly. The blocker was circumstance, not a platform limit.

findings-against-prior-runs.finding: The Semantica export bridge has never been run with real content.
findings-against-prior-runs.detail: .ai-raccoon/semantica-graph.json is tracked and was committed containing the export script's empty DEFAULT_SEED. Combined with the skill's own 'no import_graph mechanism exists', the project has tooling to carry decisions across Semantica sessions that has neither been exercised nor could be loaded back if it were.
